approachQuestion.prompt:
Balanced Four-Team Roster

A roster string uses only A, B, C, D, and its length n is divisible by four. You may choose one contiguous substring and replace its characters arbitrarily with the same number of characters. Return the minimum substring length needed to make each letter occur exactly n/4 times in the whole roster. Choosing an empty substring is allowed.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; n is divisible by four.
• Only one substring may be replaced; its length stays unchanged. Return a length without changing the input.

Examples:
1. roster = "AAAABBCD" → 2: replacing two adjacent As by C and D yields two of each letter.
2. roster = "ABCD" → 0.
3. roster = "" → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; n is divisible by four.
Only one substring may be replaced; its length stays unchanged. Return a length without changing the input.

options.text: Count letters outside the candidate replacement window. Find the shortest window for which every outside count is at most n/4, decrementing outside counts on extension and incrementing them on shrinking. Return zero immediately if already balanced.
options.feedback: Outside letters cannot change. If none exceed its quota, the missing counts exactly fill the replaceable window, so a replacement exists.

options.text: Binary-search the shortest length permitting a valid replacement, checking all windows of each trial length with four outside counts. Handle already-balanced input as zero.
options.feedback: A feasible window can be extended to any larger length, so feasibility is monotone, but repeated passes are unnecessary with one shrinking cover window.

options.text: Return only the sum of positive excesses above n/4 across letters, regardless of their positions.
options.feedback: For roster "ABACADAA", n=8 and A occurs five times, so three As must be replaced. No length-three segment contains three As; at least four positions are required. Total surplus alone ignores their separation.

options.text: Find the shortest substring containing one occurrence of every currently underrepresented letter. Replace it and return its length.
options.feedback: For "AAAA", B,C,D are absent, so no such substring exists, yet replacing any three positions balances the roster.

feedback.reason: Only letters inside the replacement window may change.
details: Count all four letters. If each count equals n/4 return zero. Treat counts as those outside an initially empty window. Extend right by decrementing its letter. While every outside count is at most n/4, update the shortest length, then increment the outgoing left letter and advance left.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Track the unchangeable outside” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Four outside counts and monotone boundaries give linear work.
details: Necessity follows because outside letters remain. Sufficiency follows since quota deficits sum to exactly the window length, so it can be filled to meet them. Expanding a window only decreases outside counts, making shrink-while-feasible safe. Four counters and forward boundaries give linear time and constant auxiliary storage.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each window move updates one of four outside counts, and shrinking advances the left index only n times total.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The four quotas need neither sorting nor an n-entry frequency structure.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Counts are indexed by four team letters, not roster positions; replacing windows are retained only as boundaries.
